children: The Bombay High Court ruled that execution proceedings cannot be kept alive after the underlying arbitral award has been set aside merely because an appeal is pending before the Supreme Court.

The Bombay High Court has held that an execution petition cannot be kept pending when the arbitral award sought to be enforced has already been set aside, merely because an appeal against that decision is pending before the Supreme Court.

Justice N.J. Jamadar allowed a writ petition filed by JSW Steel Ltd challenging an order of the District Judge, Alibag-Raigad, which had declined to dismiss execution proceedings initiated by Krunal Engineering Works.

The proceedings arose from an award dated 8 May 2015 passed by the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council, Konkan Region. The respondent had instituted Darkhast No. 188 of 2016 to enforce the award.

JSW Steel submitted that a Division Bench of the High Court had set aside the award by its judgment dated 4 October 2021. Although the award-holder challenged that decision before the Supreme Court and notice was issued in the matter, no stay had been granted on the operation of the High Court’s judgment.

The District Judge had nevertheless kept the execution petition pending, observing that Civil Appeal No. 1016 of 2025 was awaiting adjudication before the Supreme Court and that dismissing the proceedings before the appeal was decided would not be in the interest of justice.
Rejecting this approach, the High Court observed that, as matters presently stood, there was no award capable of being executed.
“The fact remains that there is no Award that can be executed,” the Court stated.

It further noted that if the respondent ultimately succeeded before the Supreme Court and the award was restored, the execution proceedings could be revived. Consequently, the Court found no propriety in keeping the execution petition alive after the underlying award had been set aside.
The High Court accordingly disposed of the execution petition while granting the respondent liberty to revive it if the judgment setting aside the award is reversed or set aside by the Supreme Court.
Dr Abhinav Chandrachud, along with Sneha Jaisingh, Akshay Ayush and Sannidhi Agrawal, instructed by Bharucha & Partners, appeared for JSW Steel.
Advocates Gauri K. Jadhav, Sneha M. Dhatrak and Krutika Kharat represented the respondent.
